keyframe_review.note: 77,500 km2 for 592-910 (Tamil Nadu 213 cells, southern Kerala 73) is the Pandya core, a single flat shape for 318 years; the infobox has no area. The page has expansions Cliopatria does not draw: Sendan 'expanding his kingdom to the Chera country' (c. 620-650), Varagunavarman I (c. 765-815) who 'conquered the Kongu country', and the liberation of Venadu in 825. The 592 shape stands for 592-764 only; the next three keyframes carry 765-915. ledger.note: 825: Venad is free. 'The Kollam Era is said to mark the liberation of Venadu from Pandya control' in 825 CE.

region.text: the Kongu country, Coimbatore and Salem (the gazetteer lacks 'Kongu Nadu')

ledger.note: c. 897: Kongu goes to the Cholas. 'By c. 897 CE, Chola king Aditya I was the master of the old Pallava, Ganga and Kongu countries'. The year is the page's 'c. 897'.

910: Parantaka I takes Madurai. 'Parantaka I invaded the Pandya territories in 910 CE and captured Madurai'; the Parantaka page: 'He captured the Pandyan capital early in his reign' and had the title Maturai Kontan 'by the third year' (907 + 3). Hatched; the Pandya king still holds the rest.

c. 915: the Pandya king loses at Vellur. 'The decisive battle appears to have taken place at Vellur around 915'; 'this victory was narrow'; Parantaka 'completed his conquest of the entire Pandya country' (undated). The occupation turns into annexation.

region.text: the Pandya country: Madurai, Tirunelveli and the south, taken by the Cholas

ledger.note: c. 915: the Pandya kingdom is conquered. 'Then the Pandya king fled into exile in Sri Lanka' (Rajasimha II; the year is silent on the page; Kassapa V of Anuradhapura 'sent an army to his aid'). Cliopatria runs the row to 921.

wars.name: Pandya-Pallava wars
wars.outcome: Arikesari Maravarman (c. 640-670) 'known for his battles against the Pallavas of Kanchi'; Maravarman Rajasimha I (c. 710-765) 'threatened Pallava king Nandivarman II Pallavamalla'; Varagunavarman I (c. 765-815) 'invaded the Pallava country'. The page names no battle date or treaty and no land changing hands.
wars.note: The page is silent on Pennagadam, Sankaramangai, Pazhayarai, Kudamukku/Venbai, Tellaru and Arisil.

wars.name: Pandya conquest of Kongu

zones.text: the Kongu country, Coimbatore and Salem (the gazetteer lacks 'Kongu Nadu')

wars.outcome: Varagunavarman I conquered the Kongu country; it passed to the Cholas by c. 897.

wars.name: Pandya-Sinhalese wars of the 9th century
wars.outcome: Srimara Srivallabha (815-862) 'sailed to Sri Lanka, subjugated and overpowered King Sena I' (undated); Sena II then 'invaded the Pandya country, sacked Madurai' (undated) and Varaguna II was chosen king; Varaguna II suffered a crushing defeat near Kumbakonam c. 880. No land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Chola conquest of the Pandya country
wars.outcome: Parantaka I captured Madurai in 910 and won the decisive battle at Vellur c. 915; Rajasimha II fled to Sri Lanka and the whole Pandya country became Chola.
wars.note: The Chola dossier (sa-03) may date the end differently; Cliopatria's Pandya row runs to 921.

certainty.note: The page gives regions and reigns only; the Kongu and Venad limits are reigns, not borders.

notes: Two pages. Wikidata Q844910 is shared with pandya-empire (Cliopatria 1216-1325, owned by sa-04): both are the Pandya dynasty, whose infobox runs 400 BCE-1618 CE. They are treated here as different states (no Cliopatria shape between 921 and 1216; a Chola eclipse of c. 300 years, the Second Pandya Empire of 1216-1345 being a revival); this dossier lists only 'Pandya Dynasty' in cliopatria_names. The colour agent should give pandya-empire this family and hue (rule 2: the same dynasty). early-pandyas (sa-02, -291..305) is the earlier phase. The page has no area and no 'Early Pandyas/Empire' labels. Kadungon c. 560-590 and Avanisulamani c. 590-620 fix the revival only by reigns; Cliopatria's 592 and the kalabhra dossier's 592 loss are used (confidence 1). The dissolve is 915 (Vellur 'around 915'), not Cliopatria's 921: Madurai fell c. 910 and the flight is undated; sa-03's chola-empire dossier should date the gain of the Pandya country to match (910 occupation, 915 annexation). The Kongu, Venad and Sri Lanka passages are reign-dated only; Cliopatria's flat 77,500 km2 for 318 years is the core, and the three new keyframes are the researcher's reading of them (confidence 1-2). The page does not name the victor at Kumbakonam c. 880 (Pallava Aparajita with Chola Aditya I in other accounts, not read here), so no war is listed. Gazetteer: 'Kongu Nadu' and 'Venad' are not regions (Coimbatore and Salem radii, Kerala within the shape, used).
